title: refactor(channels): deslop channel lifecycle
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Channel integrations repeat binding projection, accepted-receipt accumulation, and Markdown offset mechanics, while some preview paths maintain redundant state and forwarding layers.

## User Impact

Configuration, persisted schemas, binding identity and expiry, message formatting, and streaming behavior stay the same. Two runtime-replacement defects are also fixed: Zalo uses the current runtime's media store, and an old Synology response cannot free a replacement runtime's serving slot. No migration or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing binding owner now supplies pure record projection and account-prefixed adapter dispatch. Matrix keeps its parent-room grammar; all plugins keep storage, expiry, mutation authority, and stop settlement. The existing delivery-result owner accumulates native accepted sends for Matrix, Mattermost, and iMessage, preserving their receipts and accepted content. Feishu and Telegram retain their distinct logical merge rules.

Markdown Core supplies one UTF-16 edit/offset operation for Teams, iMessage, and plain-text projection. Teams loses redundant native state and forwarding helpers; Mattermost's turn owner handles preview boundaries directly and represents disabled previews with an optional draft. Existing stronger boundary tests replace the removed helper-only tests.

The measured batch removes **337 net production lines** (569 added, 906 deleted), including replacement helpers and the two fixes. Tests add 59 net lines and docs add 23; neither is counted as production savings. This is the exhausted-scope below-1000 batch: all 49 surveyed files plus the SDK offset owners and CI repair owners were read, and the coverage log follows. Shared hosted-media extraction was withheld while another consolidation owned its SDK file; that work has since merged separately. No new persistence, namespace, retention, or streaming policy is introduced.

Canonical mock-baseline regeneration removes one obsolete suppression after migrating the Mattermost mock. That shrink-only follow-up has a clean isolated review.

## Removed Zero-Consumer SDK Exports

The three new public exports are offset in this same PR by removing six public callable helpers. The last three also offset SDK growth inherited from the conflict-only rebase:

- `allow-from`: `mapBasicAllowlistResolutionEntries`.
- `extension-shared`: `runStoppablePassiveMonitor`.
- `json-store`: `readJsonFileWithFallback`.
- `gateway-runtime`: `resolveAdvertisedLanHost`.
- `provider-auth`: `normalizeSecretInputModeInput`.
- `computer-use`: `compileComputerUseValidator`.

Repository-wide source/test/doc searches found only their declarations. Dynamic and namespace consumers were inspected; none selects, enumerates, or calls these names. None appears in the [published documentation corpus](https://docs.openclaw.ai/llms-full.txt), checked on 2026-10-05. Unused wrapper imports and the private monitor type are also removed; Teams still consumes `BasicAllowlistResolutionEntry`, so that type remains.

Canonical SDK surface result: **3,648 public exports and 2,110 callable exports**. The original counts were 3,652 / 2,113. The final conflict-only rebase inherited main at 3,651 / 2,114; this PR removes three exports and four callables relative to that base. Both caps are tightened to the canonical counts; no cap increased.

## Fixes Found Along the Way

- Zalo cached the first runtime's store indefinitely. Switching to a runtime with another state directory could still serve the old runtime's capability. The cache now follows runtime identity while preserving persisted entries and consume-on-GET behavior.
- Copilot could start an isolated-completion send before a cancellation queued at its boundary. The deferred operation now starts only after the canonical timeout owner registers cancellation; the existing boundary regression fails before the fix.
- Synology cleared shared limiter maps on replacement, allowing old cleanup to decrement a new runtime's count. Preparation, serving, and bandwidth operations now retain their original runtime-owned instances across awaits and cleanup. All limits and deadlines are unchanged.

## Evidence

Exact-head hosted CI `37309832567` completed with two inherited wrapper-tooling failures and their downstream gate. `eager-import-closure.test.ts` (job `111762809806`, two cases) and `pr-worktree-provision.test.ts` (job `111762809732`, three cases) fail because main's new `deferred-plugin-migrations.contract.ts` is missing from the protected wrapper inventory. Independent current-head QA Lab PR #165554, [run 37310598515/job 111765229028](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37310598515/job/111765229028), reproduces all five exact failures on the same main base. None of the failing inputs or inventory paths is changed here. `openclaw/ci-gate` job `111766711834` only propagates those two roots. All touched-area checks and both hosted cycle checks passed. The coordinator-authorized exact-head admin exception applies; the complete per-job attribution is recorded in the evidence comment.

The second hosted run (`37295034449`) passed the first-round repairs but exposed four failing cases in Codex and Copilot. Linux replay on the rebased parent reproduced all four (68 passed, 4 failed; 123.51 seconds). Copilot now passes a lazy operation factory to the canonical timeout owner, restoring abort-listener-before-send ordering; its existing regression is unchanged. Codex fixtures acknowledge the exact unsubscribe after terminal cleanup, retain pre-cleanup non-settlement assertions, and verify exactly-once unsubscribe and client survival. Failed interruption still retires the client, and terminal-RPC failure still rejects. The existing subscription suite retains sibling-survival and thread-reuse proof. Independent review of these repairs and the additional removals is scoped-clean at P1/P2.

**BELOW-1000** with complete survey coverage below. Final head: `d61f1b7555d2`; rebased base: `bd64d93ff1ae`. The coordinator accepted the BELOW-1000 batch and authorized publication with zero runtime cycles and no new Madge component relative to clean main. Original base: `48c08e6ccba6`. No cap increased.

- Linux / Node 26.5.0 / frozen pnpm 12.5.1 install: final `d61f1b7555d2` passes core and extension production types, extension test types, focused cancellation/subscription/SDK tests (**83 tests / 4 files / 122.31 seconds**), and the final fixture/ratchet lint with zero warnings/errors. The previous `f1e9c1cda67c` passed all 27 consuming core test graphs, **1,436 focused/contract tests / 63 files / 353.56 seconds**, and the full build in **10 minutes 44.4 seconds**. Commands use `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ... --maxWorkers=1`.
- Runtime-value cycles: **0**. Candidate and clean base reproduce the same single Madge component; no changed path participates. The coordinator authorized this unchanged-component comparison, and peer main commit `21901766c534` now breaks the cycle with a leaf migration contract. The prepared candidate merges cleanly with fresh main; no rebase was needed. Hosted guard job `111762808014` confirms zero runtime-value cycles and zero Madge cycles with that repair included. No ignore or cap increase was used.
- SDK surface tooling verifies **3,648 public exports / 2,110 callables**. Canonical declaration baselines were regenerated for `bd64d93ff1ae` → `d61f1b7555d2`: three additions, six removals, zero direct signature changes, digest `c1e7a313`. The tool also marks 128 unchanged direct exports as reachable because the unused computer-use compiler and its private types disappeared from their declaration closure; the complete namespace declaration diff contains only that removal.
- Zalo's regression failed before repair (200 instead of 404), then passed. Synology's deterministic fake-clock regression failed before repair (200 instead of 503 after old-response completion), then passed in the database-backed suite. These exercise actual media-handler/store boundaries; namespaces, deadlines and limits are unchanged.
- Independent review completed for the production consolidation, unused-export removal, and final caller/lint fixes. Two initial review findings were rejected against owner source: partial errors require visible acceptance, and Teams still clears deferred replacement entries in `finally`. No actionable finding remains.

Verification caught two stale Mattermost test callers and six lint errors; all were fixed and replayed on the final head without weakening assertions, goldens or rules. Two earlier Mac host-hook cases crossed the existing retirement deadline under heavy host load; the Linux replay passes without changing that deadline or claiming a flake fix. The first hosted run also exposed a serialized-key-order regression and three CI contracts: the shared binding projection now preserves the worker’s exact conversation byte order, the SDK callable cap is pinned to the smaller source count, the Mattermost mock preserves real exports, and the Teams reasoning-end callback is awaited. The unchanged byte-identity regression and 1,259 affected tests/contracts pass (53 files, 238.84 seconds). The obsolete mock baseline entry was removed by its canonical prune tool. The Telegram media fixture failure in that run was separately repaired on main by `6c21f5affcbe` (#165430); this PR does not duplicate it. All five Telegram cases passed in the second hosted run.

title: fix: preserve requests in generic and 5xx failures
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Generic and provider-5xx assistant failures currently report that execution failed without preserving the user's request in the response contract or stating whether replay is safe. That leaves users unsure whether to repeat the request, risks duplicate side effects when earlier actions may have completed, and makes `/new` a potentially destructive recovery path.

This change preserves the original request in the conversation-facing failure copy, explicitly states that automatic replay was withheld, and tells the user to verify possible side effects before retrying.

## Summary

- preserve the original user request in generic and 5xx assistant failure messages
- state whether replay is safe instead of returning a context-free error
- provide an actionable recovery path
- add focused failure-copy coverage and update affected execution tests

## Evidence

- 136/136 focused tests passed:
  - `src/agents/failover/assistant-request-failure-copy.test.ts`
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-failure-reply.test.ts`
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-provider-failures.test.ts`
- formatter completed on all five changed files
- `git diff --check` passed
- regression expectations were updated at the actual execution path, not only the helper
- commit: `3d02b6fd196e8534219f9401ca7eca2b814ec445`

## Risk

Scoped to user-facing failure copy and its focused tests. No provider-routing or retry-policy changes.

title: perf(gateway): serve chat message and usage RPC reads from workers
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening individual chat messages and usage reports can run session lookups, store discovery, and transcript scans on the Gateway main thread.

## Why This Change Was Made

Serve `chat.message.get` through the existing history row preparation and synchronous sharing checks. Move usage store discovery, selected context reports, and transcript hydration through the existing shared-state and history readers.

List and exact-report requests carry their captured physical identity into the worker and retain the native source receipt through consumption. Multi-store reports retain every store before the first read yields. Report publication checks current session and requester facts, including role-cache invalidation, without host SQL.

## User Impact

The five measured message/usage variants perform zero main-thread SQL. Response shapes, stored transcript bytes, schemas, configuration, and update behavior stay unchanged. The synchronous combined-store SDK view remains for the public contract shipped in [v2026.9.8](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.8/src/plugin-sdk/session-transcript-hit.ts#L24). Metadata/model-list migration is a separate follow-up; inbox behavior is outside this change.

Production diff: **+499/−277, net +222** (776 changed lines across 15 production files). No new `OPENCLAW_*` names, database service, persistent cache, schema, or durability policy.

## Evidence

An isolated Gateway used two synthetic sessions, four mock-provider turns, six messages in the primary session, and a populated synthetic inbox. Each of 20 supported RPC scenarios ran once cold and ten more times; **220/220 requests succeeded**. Native `exec/get/all/run/iterate` calls were counted per phase and attributed by caller; prepares were recorded separately. Calibration observed seven executed statements and two prepares on both main and worker threads. Startup/connect/shutdown are separate phases. These are statement counts, not latency measurements or claims about total SQL work. Baseline main-thread attribution ranked worker-migratable agent admission/schema checks (346), audit migration checks (92 at the top site), readonly opens and metadata reads (79 each), transcript scans (72), exact entry reads (66 at each of two sites), and deletion discovery (66). These are observed site counts across the five selected cold/repeated phases; phase windows can include concurrent work.

| RPC | Cold MAIN SQL, before → after | MAIN SQL across ten repeated calls, before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `chat.message.get` | 15 → 0 | 150 → 0 |
| `sessions.usage`, all agents | 60 → 0 | 377 → 0 |
| `sessions.usage`, selected key | 34 → 0 | 371 → 0 |
| Usage timeseries | 442 → 0 | 90 → 0 |
| Usage logs | 9 → 0 | 96 → 0 |
| **Total** | **560 → 0** | **1,084 → 0** |

Approved-head measurement: commit `bf5be347b276b88014a2da3bdb33451144245399`; 216.08s wall time; every disk database remained inside the synthetic fixture; graceful exit 0. The selected RPC phases also recorded zero main-thread prepares and failed SQL attempts. Two main-thread `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` busy attempts occurred during connection and one worker busy attempt during audit pruning at shutdown; all are outside the measured RPC phases, and the run completed successfully.

Regressions fail on the pre-correction implementations for the intended reasons: valid legacy file-symlink discovery being refused; native SQL in the moved paths; reports surviving revocation; file replacement/restore during real worker reads; a later store closing while an earlier read settles; and role-cache invalidation causing the final guard to query on the host. Positive checks preserve physical ownership, current access, and close/reopen behavior.

The database-worker ratchet passed against the pinned base with no T1 call-count growth. Boundary tests prove zero caller-thread SQL for the moved operations.

SDK receipt `418aebb2`: no added/removed entrypoints or direct export-signature changes. Four reachable internal module declarations changed, affecting 128 transitive exports: combined-store extraction/type exports, moved list request/reply types, optional identity/source facts on existing worker contracts, and their updated type imports. The released synchronous combined-store helper remains intact; no Gateway context service signature changed.

The worker-cutover importer audit found affected suites already assigned to host-owned fork projects; no routing change was needed. Indirect proof includes project recents, message-get archive/global/oversize/branch behavior, live/RPC avatar parity, plugin metadata cleanup, and account deletion/reconnect settlement. The slower cases exercise real worker transport, file identity, committed publication, and lifecycle settlement; mock-only checks cannot establish those contracts. Final-head CI results and timings are recorded below.

A local preparation attempt hit `ENOENT` while the runtime build replaced a package output directory. Builds and tests were then serialized and the affected suites rerun. A later check overlapped dependency preparation and produced cascading implicit-any errors because its Vitest declaration chunks were absent from the captured type graph. The isolated graph recheck passed in 15.85s with all seven chunks restored; final check results are listed above.

Retained synchronous paths are explicitly scoped: the released SDK view above; projection-backed project recents (`src/gateway/server-methods/projects.ts:409`, using the existing ready projection and federation/incognito handling); and unchanged project-checkout deletion reference checks (`projects.ts:331`, called at `:617`). title: chore(deps): update fs-safe to 0.23.1 and simplify copies
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Updates OpenClaw to fs-safe 0.23.1 so container clone refusals and gVisor file creation use the dependency's fixes, and removes OpenClaw's temporary clone-fallback adapter.

Related: #165257, #164113.

## User Impact

Retained updater files and candidate plugin snapshots keep copying when a container denies FICLONE. Fresh installs on gVisor benefit from the corrected no-replace publication fallback. Native-required mode remains fail-closed for unavailable publication capabilities, and genuine I/O errors remain fatal.

The installed updater owns the first update hop: an affected 2026.9.7 installation still needs a manual npm install of a fixed release. Later drivers inherit the copy fix through fs-safe 0.23.1 or newer.

## Why This Change Was Made

fs-safe now owns FICLONE capability detection and guarded byte fallback. This removes the application adapter, syscall-message matching, sticky clone-disable state, once-per-operation warning, obsolete mock scenarios, and its PR-wrapper inventory entry. Ordinary copies call `Root.copyIn` directly with `clone: "auto"`.

SQLite retains its independent disk-space contract. When a caller supplies `beforeByteCopy`, it first requests a required clone; only a normalized cloning-capability refusal can lead to space admission and a byte copy. fs-safe has no public callback before automatic byte fallback, so using `auto` there would bypass admission or unnecessarily reject low-space reflinks. The narrow cloning-unavailable message check also prevents a no-replace publication refusal from being mistaken for a clone refusal.

All source identity and inventory checks, create-only publication, caller-selected durability, restrictive modes, byte bounds, hardlink policies, concurrent-copy draining, and the SQLite publication receipt remain. A failure after publication never triggers another copy. Existing snapshot verification and rollback ownership remain unchanged.

**Net 105 lines removed:** 50 production lines, 54 test lines, and one tooling inventory line. The 68-line adapter is deleted. SQLite's admitted byte limit, receipt, identity checks, and meaningful admission/publication tests are retained.

No caller migration; required-native publication still fails closed. SQLite does not retry unrelated capability errors. |

title: perf(gateway): reuse admitted state during process bootstrap
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway startup loads plugin Doctor rules that valid configuration does not use, and config-recovery/pending-migration reads leave the already admitted SQLite snapshot. That adds module-loading and snapshot work before the listener can bind, and can mix database generations during one inspection.

Related: #165218.

## User Impact

Startup does less work while preserving invalid-config repair guidance, migration admission, and current-state checks before writes. No new settings, persistent cache, schema migration, or update action is required.

The campaign target of listening within 10 seconds and ready within 15 seconds remains **unmet**. These synthetic measurements do not prove production deployment timing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Config-health and deferred-plugin reads now use the existing snapshot-aware read worker. Their old writer-actor read operations are removed. Health observations retain their captured database/environment, supersession and error behavior, and compare-and-swap write basis. The two admission passes remain: startup must recheck after acquiring the migration lease.

Valid startup no longer evaluates unused Doctor advisory rules. Invalid startup and explicit Doctor inspections retain them. Generic metadata completion replaces the redundant Doctor wrapper; separate include/complete flags that callers always passed together are removed.

The requested production LOC filter reports **108 insertions / 110 deletions (net −2)**. Excluding its included test harness and test-ratchet row, implementation alone is net −5 lines.

## Evidence

Three regression categories failed on the original implementation: valid startup executed an unused Doctor module, and both async state readers observed a later foreign commit inside an earlier admission snapshot. The new tests also prove stale recovery cannot overwrite that foreign commit and invalid config retains plugin repair advice. CPU profiles identify plugin module resolution/loading as a large baseline cost.

### Measurement

Five alternating warm samples per version on the same Blacksmith Testbox, Node 24.19.0, base `599bcd79e5ae` versus this patch. Each built version runs from the same `dist/index.js` path; warm-up runs are excluded.

| Measurement | Before, median | After, median | Before range | After range |

| Started → ready | 23.168 s | 14.730 s | 16.962–27.782 s | 12.602–17.733 s |

The fixture has **38 loaded plugins** (37 synthetic plugins plus memory-core), two agents, 810 worktree-shaped directories, approximately 510 MiB of shared SQLite padding, and an existing config backup. The directories are fixture shape; admission does not scan arbitrary worktrees. State is synthetic, plugins do not reproduce a production import graph, and the listener binds only to loopback. Small samples and variable timings limit extrapolation.

Earlier exploratory Node 26 rig measurements used `dist/entry.js` and 39 loaded plugins: listening 26.845 → 19.901 s, ready 36.441 → 25.919 s, CLI bootstrap 8.420 → 3.793 s (five-sample medians). A corrected `dist/index.js` rig comparison was confounded by rising concurrent load; its attempted alternating rebuild was killed by host OOM while disk was full. ### Proof

Fixes Windows Gateway status rejecting a freshly installed service's runtime pin when its Scheduled Task supplies the working directory.

## User Impact

A successful explicit Node or Bun install keeps a valid runtime pin on the next status inspection. Status still reports the actual effective working directory. Existing pins remain usable without reinstalling the service or rewriting runtime intent.

Superseded by the merged upstream startup work in #165218 (`ddf95b6c52db452426f56a62d46962284b2d5f31`). Closing this candidate after inspecting current `origin/main` at `98c200e21de`; its head was not merged.

title: fix(ui): steer messages jump into the middle of an active run, then disappear
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a steer message sent during an active run shows up in the middle of the transcript (above tool activity and text that were already visible), then disappears before its saved copy arrives.

## User Impact

User impact: a steer moves once from the queue to the bottom of the transcript when delivery starts and stays there until its saved copy replaces it. Everything that was already visible stays above it, new output appears below it, and that order survives history refreshes, reconnects, pane remounts, and reloading a finished run, including when a streamed answer spans the steer.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three independent defects produced the reported behavior:

- **Live placement (Control UI).** Already-visible tool rows without a paired text segment never received the steer boundary in `chat-thread-build.ts`, so timestamp placement reordered `tool -> answer -> steer` into `answer -> steer -> tool`. When a steer is delivered, every live tool of that run that is already visible is now closed before it (`closeToolStreamBoundary` in `tool-stream-state.ts`), tools that start afterward record the steer as their lower boundary, and the thread builder prefers those recorded boundaries; stream reconciliation keeps them through history and terminal reconciliation.
- **Persisted order (Codex harness).** The native event projector excluded unfinished assistant items from the pre-steer snapshot, so text streamed before the steer was saved after it, combined with the continuation. The projector now captures the already-streamed prefix at steer delivery, persists it before the steer, and persists only the continuation afterward (`event-projector-steering.ts`). The transcript mirror tracks committed segments per candidate so a changed completion identity, raw completions, repeated steering, and partial-write retries cannot drop or duplicate the continuation. Existing transcript tables and columns; no schema change.
- **Disappearance (Control UI).** Accepting queued custody or input consumption retired the optimistic steer display before the canonical transcript copy existed. Dispatched steers are now retained through the existing submission owner until their transcript receipt replaces them exactly once, including across cache remounts; cancelled or stopped inputs still retire immediately, and failed sends still hand Retry to the outbox row.

title: fix(gateway): steering during worktree creation still runs as a follow-up after the task
body:
Related: #165462

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a message sent with Steer right after starting a New Session with a new worktree (while it shows "Creating worktree…") still runs as a separate follow-up turn after the task finishes, instead of reaching the task. #165462 fixed a later point in that window; live, the steer usually arrives while the first turn's reply operation exists but its backend is still preparing.

## User Impact

User impact: steering during worktree creation now joins the first turn as soon as its runtime is ready, on both the built-in and the Codex runtime. If that turn ends, is replaced, or its authority changes first, the message still runs once as a follow-up. The queued-follow-up acknowledgement semantics are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runActiveReplySteer` resolved the injection target and the steering authority when the steer was admitted. During preparation the active reply operation has no ready backend yet, so there was no target and the steer fell back to the follow-up queue immediately. The steering owner now parks the input in its FIFO custody, waits for that exact reply operation's backend to become ready (new readiness signal on the reply-run registry), then re-verifies the same operation object, resolves tool/pending-input authority at that moment, and injects. Cancellation, retirement, and rekeying release the wait and fall back. Authority is revalidated after the wait and immediately before injection rather than captured beforehand.

## Evidence

Live (dev Gateway, OpenAI provider, fresh state): `sessions.create {worktree: true, message}` then `chat.send {queueMode: "steer", message: "…put the word PINEAPPLE<n>…"}` ~2 s later, while the worktree was being created.

| Build | Runs | Steer position in transcript | Final answer contains the word |

| main 500c95aa, Codex runtime | 2 (follow-up) | after the answer | no |

title: perf(gateway): exit interrupted restarts after database close
body:
## What Problem This Solves

An external restart could leave the Gateway unavailable until its shutdown deadline while plugin teardown remained stuck, even after its final clean-close database receipt was durable.

## User Impact

After an external restart exhausts its active-work drain, the predecessor exits once required persistence and database closure settle. Normal drain allowances, terminal persistence protection, WAL/receipt admission, and the supervisor deadline remain intact. No configuration, schema, or update migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The process-owning CLI supplies an exit continuation only for an external restart whose drain timed out. The existing close owner joins final chat writes and Memory's database borrows, closes agent databases, and keeps their admission fence through boot-outcome persistence, bounded local-service cleanup, lock release, and log flushing. Remaining plugin/channel teardown no longer retains that process. Required cleanup phases log elapsed milliseconds.

A receipt belongs to one physical database. Accepted restart-marker writes can reopen it and invalidate an earlier receipt, so the proof measures the final durable receipt and also reports the first. The exit decision uses the existing all-database close owner, not receipt-log observation.

Production LOC: **+111** (`197 added / 86 removed`, excluding tests/support/docs). The old CLI log-flush module is removed and its callers move to one exit-bookkeeping module. Growth carries the process host's exit authority, preserves the database fence through exit, and records bounded bookkeeping. Fixes #161769

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a subagent completion into a session that restart recovery resumed fails `SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED` on every retry (about one failed gateway `agent` attempt per minute) while the recovered turn stays live, instead of queueing behind it.

## User Impact

User impact: after a gateway restart, subagent completions for a resumed orchestrator or dashboard session wait for the recovered turn and run as the next turn, as they do for any busy requester. The retry-failure log noise stops, and there is no retry-backoff delay (up to a few minutes) after the recovered turn ends. The existing announce delivery window is unchanged: a recovered turn that outlives it still expires the completion, the same as an ordinary busy requester.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runWithAgentCommandRecoveryOwner` already waits for a live restart-recovery owner, re-prepares and re-claims, but only for `subagent_settle` (#140930). Subagent completion announces carry `subagent_announce` and took the reject path. The change adds `subagent_announce` to that gate only. It keeps the ownerless, tombstoned, replaced, rerouted, aborted and generation checks. It holds no lease while waiting and does not extend any deadline. This matches docs/concepts/session.md: once recovery starts, messages follow the session's normal queue policy.

## What Problem This Solves

## Why This Change Was Made

Make the canonical trajectory recorder and sink factories asynchronous and move durable target preparation into the existing ordered session reader. Capture the physical store, normalized target, and environment before yielding; consume the exact row inside writer FIFO custody and carry the selected database identity into sink construction. Preserve complete targets whose session row has not committed yet, conflicting-mapping rejection, and legacy-marker validation.

Fence ordered reads against synchronous SDK writes using the native handle and mutation witness. The reader retains its owner through consumption and cleanup and rejects revoked results. Runtime callers revalidate current run/source authority after preparation. Append authority, FIFO receipts, accepted-work settlement, and cancellation behavior keep their existing owners. Process-held incognito state remains with its native owner.

All internal and local-test callers now await the single canonical factory. The SQLite testing subpath is private/local-only and explicitly excluded from the published package, so no synchronous compatibility facade remains.

title: fix(agents): preserve restart-interrupted parent continuation ownership
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an interrupted parent continuation loses its source identity when a Gateway restart also drains queued child announcements, allowing the original completion to run again or fail behind the recovery owner.

## User Impact

Parent turns started by subagent pause notices or completion announcements retain the same recovery source across restart. Retries join the existing recovery and consume its final receipt. Unrelated child completions wait for the recovery owner; stopping, resetting, replacing, or rerouting a session still revokes pending work.

No schema, configuration, or migration changes. Existing session recovery fields and terminal receipts retain ownership; waiting yielded parents remain with the child-batch owner. Previously persisted source-less recovery rows retain the existing single-fence correlation fallback until they settle.

## Why This Change Was Made

Shutdown previously saved the active and queued run fences, then cleared the active lifecycle ID. Startup could identify a source only when exactly one fence remained. Preserve the already-recorded source before releasing lifecycle ownership, and apply the existing receipt reconciliation to announcements as well as settle turns. Refuse execution if that exact source completed while waiting for recovery, without blocking a different sibling source.

Includes the announce admission wait from #161788, with credit to @Oldrich333. This complements #165335: restoring unrelated registry work after a superseded transfer does not preserve a parent continuation's own interrupted source. Recovery logs now identify skipped sessions and reasons even when other sessions start successfully.

title: fix(skills): recheck prerequisites when a new session starts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

If an operator installed a skill's missing prerequisite (for example, a required CLI on an existing PATH directory) after the Gateway had started, new sessions still treated that skill as ineligible. The skill never showed up for new conversations until the Gateway restarted.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/skills/runtime/session-snapshot.ts` returned a completed, cached eligibility snapshot to fresh sessions (introduced in `a3d173d4cbcb`), so prerequisite checks never re-ran. A fresh session now recomputes eligibility once, at session start. The raw discovery cache and concurrent build sharing stay in place, so there is no per-request polling.

Existing and persisted sessions hydrate only the exact skill identities they saved (name, file path, and file host) before provider precedence applies. Older snapshots without source data fall back to their recorded gateway path or prompt-catalog location. Completed projections are reused only for the same persisted selection. This matters when two skill roots provide the same name and the newly eligible provider differs: the running session keeps the implementation it snapshotted, and a new session gets the current one. One matching rule handles all of this, and no parallel source list runs through the loader. This matches the rule that prompt-state changes take effect in the next session.

## User Impact

Installing a skill's prerequisite makes the skill available in the next new session without a Gateway restart. Running sessions keep their existing skill prompt.

## Evidence

- Real session entry-point regression: install the required binary into an existing PATH directory, then start a new session. It failed before the fix and passes after.
- Six provider-switch regressions and three node/local collision cases, each with two providers of the same skill name, failed on earlier drafts and pass now. The existing session keeps its provider, and a new session sees the current one.
- 1,257 skills and consumer tests pass, with one Windows-only skip. The changed gate's components pass; its two Knip scans timed out when run concurrently under local load and passed sequentially. Remote proof was unavailable because of a Testbox admission stall, an AWS capacity refusal, and a Hetzner transfer stall, so exact-head CI is the final gate.

title: fix(gateway): crash-interrupted sessions never resume while agent databases finish startup admission
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a Gateway crash (SIGKILL, power loss, OOM), interrupted sessions are never resumed or settled when their agent database is still finishing startup inspection; they stay `running` forever and the Control UI shows them as idle with no notice that the task stopped.

## User Impact

User impact: work interrupted by a hard crash now resumes automatically once each agent database finishes its post-crash admission, as `docs/gateway/restart-recovery.md` already promises. Healthy agents recover without waiting for slower databases. No config, schema, or protocol change.

## Why This Change Was Made

After an unclean shutdown every agent database goes through background startup inspection (stale lease from the dead writer). Main-session restart recovery starts right after `ready`, its store discovery skips databases that are still pending admission, and the scheduler treated that empty scan (zero failures) as completion. Nothing ever rescanned, so the crash-interrupted rows were never marked or resumed.

Recovery now waits on the admission owner's existing per-database completion and rescans when each pending database settles. The existing cutoffs, ownership checks, deduplication, durable retry budget, and shutdown cancellation are unchanged; waiting for admission does not consume the retry budget.

## Evidence

Live, isolated dev Gateway (macOS, OpenAI provider, one agent on the built-in runtime and one on the Codex runtime), two sessions mid-turn, Gateway SIGKILLed, then restarted with the same state:

- `main` (bbaabd6ced15): both agent databases report "has not completed startup inspection", admission finishes ~4 s after `ready`, and restart recovery logs nothing at all. Three interrupted sessions stayed `running` with no new run for the lifetime of that process.
- This branch: `agent database recovered after background inspection and preparation` (+2 s after `ready`) followed by `marked 1 startup-orphaned main session(s)` and `started interrupted main session: agent:main:dashboard:…`; the Codex-runtime session is marked as well and resumes after the first recovered run (recovery admits one run at a time, unchanged).

Regression (fails on main, passes here):

```text
TMPDIR=/private/tmp/oc-crash-recovery pnpm test src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-admission.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
main:   2 failed | 7 passed (51.9 s wall, incl. worker prep)
branch: 9 passed (39.4 s wall)
```

Also passed: `main-session-restart-recovery-marking.test.ts`, `server-agent-database-startup.preparation.test.ts` (27 tests), the scheduling/startup subset of `main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts` (20 tests), `pnpm tsgo:core`, the core test typegraph lane, targeted oxlint, and `git diff --check`.

Production: +46/−27 (most of it re-indenting the retry loop into the rescan loop); tests +152; docs +6.

<details><summary>Follow-ups seen in the same crash run (not changed here)</summary>

- memory-core dreaming startup cleanup and `restart-sentinel` ("Shared-state read admission closed") also ran before admission finished and failed; cron convergence and maintenance already retry.
- Startup recovery admits one recovered run at a time, so the Nth interrupted session waits for the previous recovered turns to finish.

</details>

The publication cache discarded every row when either the projection-wide sharing revision or reconstructed read-context object changed. Both advance for unrelated updates. Remove those blanket resets and retain the existing row-owned facts and recipient signatures. Include the current live model in those facts so a model switch within the same run still publishes a fresh row. Model filtering freezes its shallow field-removal copy and shares the already frozen nested snapshot.

title: fix: keep permit waiters until their actual deadline
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Queued work can be refused before its absolute deadline after a backward wall-clock adjustment or when a distant deadline exceeds Node's native timer range.

## User Impact

Gateway health collection can report queued account probes as timed out too early, and queued Codex inference requests can receive an early overload response. Queued permit admission now respects its original wall-clock deadline. FIFO admission, cancellation, and the caller-owned lifetime of acquired permits remain unchanged. Ordinary health deadlines are short; the oversized-deadline case protects the shared permit API.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing bounded absolute-deadline scheduler, with an opt-in unreferenced timer for permit waiters. Register waiters before scheduling so immediate expiry removes the queued entry. Simplify FIFO draining and redundant settlement bookkeeping without introducing another timer policy. The scheduler's existing callers retain their referenced timers by default.

The contributor's startup-index test fix is restored: await database-worker closure before both repair-log reads. The parent logger cannot flush worker-local queues; workers drain them before acknowledging close.
